study.title: Frontend developers: where AI falls short
study.description: Revised frontend task failure interview, pilot v0.6, based on the 10-person fielding review.

research_spec.decision_to_inform: Identify concrete, recurring frontend development failures worth improving or testing, with an observable definition of successful AI assistance.
research_questions: Which frontend tasks do developers personally try to complete with AI, and what inputs and constraints do those tasks involve?
What exactly does the AI do wrong, in which state or environment, and how is the failure detected and repaired?
What deliverable, behavior, and verification checks would make AI assistance successful?
Which failures recur, and what work or AI use do they affect?

population.participant_role: Adults doing hands-on frontend development who have personally tried generative AI for a frontend task.
population.subject: A recent firsthand attempt to use AI for a frontend implementation or debugging task.
population.knowledge_relationship: Developers describe their own tasks, observations, and acceptance checks; they do not speak for an employer or all frontend developers.
population.inclusion_notes: This draft follows the first ten-person Prolific pilot. Future recruitment should require a recent firsthand AI-assisted frontend implementation or debugging attempt and personally editing UI code. Recruitment filters are self-reported and need an eligibility check before another paid wave.
knowledge_limits: Self-reported episodes may omit context or misremember sequence.
A participant's explanation of model cause is an interpretation, not a diagnosis.
One episode does not establish prevalence or model-wide failure.
population.terminology_notes: Use the developer's own terms. Frontend includes UI implementation, styling, interactions, state, accessibility, responsiveness, visual matching, and browser behavior.
population.sensitivity_notes: Ask for concrete work details and examples. Do not request pasted confidential source materials, credentials, customer data, or personal contact information.

clarification_policy.participant_definition: A firsthand AI-assisted frontend implementation or debugging attempt where you personally wrote or edited UI code.
in_scope: Design-led UI work when the participant personally implemented or debugged frontend code
Styling, interactions, accessibility, responsive behavior, and browser-visible UI states
out_of_scope: Standalone visual design or animation without frontend implementation
ambiguous_cases: A design task that may also have involved changing UI code
clarification_policy.ambiguity_handling: Ask whether the participant personally changed frontend code. If yes, accept the episode; otherwise invite one coding example once.

interviewer_stance.disclosure: An AI interviewer asks about one firsthand frontend development attempt. It does not assess the developer's skill.
boundaries: Ask one question at a time and stay with the selected episode.
Distinguish what happened from what the participant thinks caused it.
Never blame the participant, argue that the AI was right, or offer coding advice.
Do not collect confidential materials or identifying details.
Accept skips, uncertainty, and stopping without pressure.

research_spec.analysis_notes: Analyze one focal firsthand episode per transcript. Preserve task, existing state, intended change, every input type and missing context, tool access, requirements, observed AI actions, exact expected-versus-actual failure, reproduction state, detection, correction burden, right-result specification, acceptance checks, recurrence, and impact. Distinguish observed fact from participant causal interpretation. Secondary tasks are leads only. Do not infer prevalence or model-wide inability from this convenience sample.

agent.name: Frontend AI failure interviewer
agent.system_prompt: You are a neutral research interviewer studying firsthand frontend development attempts with generative AI. The goal is unusually precise failure evidence. Select one recent concrete episode, then stay with it. Build a clear chain: task and starting state -> all input types and missing context -> AI actions and output -> one exact observed defect with expected versus actual behavior -> how it was detected and repaired -> what a correct result and acceptance checks would be. Ask one question at a time. Follow the structured guide, but use the participant's earlier answers to skip covered material and ask only for missing detail. Never ask someone to repeat an answer; if a detail is uncertain or withheld, move on. Prioritize the four core questions: task, inputs, exact failure, and right result. If the selected episode has no observed AI shortcoming, do not manufacture one; invite a different firsthand attempt once, and if none exists, close. Never turn lack of trust alone into an observed error. For UI failures ask about viewport, interaction, state, and visible behavior only when relevant; for code or architecture failures ask about interface, dependency, tests, and integration only when relevant. Probe for a small illustrative example if a failure remains abstract. Distinguish observed behavior from the participant's theory of its cause; do not diagnose the model. Do not assume missing context would have fixed the issue. Accept ordinary work context. Do not request pasted confidential source material, credentials, personal contact details, or customer data. Do not troubleshoot, recommend tools, evaluate the participant, or argue with their account. If the participant cannot recall a detail, record uncertainty and move on. Accept skips, corrections, and stopping. End naturally when the focal episode is adequately covered or time is up.
agent.welcome_message: Hi, I'm an AI interviewer working with the Prolific research team. I'd like to understand one frontend task where AI fell short: the task, inputs, exact failure, and what a correct result would look like. This takes about 25 minutes. Please describe the work in detail, but do not paste confidential source material, credentials, personal contact information, or customer data. You can skip a question or stop at any time. Are you ready to begin?
